# Observability for Spokes Access API

_last updated July 25, 2023_

## Dashboards

* [**Spokes Access API**](https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/bbd-ni3-tkq) -
  Shows performance and request rates across spokesd (frontend for Spokes
  Access API) and gitrpcd (backend on fileservers).
* [**Spokes API twirp**](https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/qay-urt-qxe) -
  Useful for investigating a cross section of Spokes Access API stats.

## Splunk

* `index=prod-spokesd` and `index=prod-gitrpcd` filter to the two services.
* `msg=request` is a per-request log. These are logged only for routed
  endpoints. These roll up a bunch of related data.

### Spokesd example

These are selected fields from a typical `msg=request` log entry from spokesd.
This example omits common log fields (e.g. `site`, `kube_namespace`, `host`).
Note that this example comes from before a change to use semantic conventions.

* `client_cert_fingerprint: 5E:81:FE:36:...` - Identifier for the client's TLS certificate (if using TLS authentication). This is useful for tracking progress of new client certificate deployment.
* `client_id: launch-production`, `tls_client: launch-production` - Identifier of the client app. This will be one of the client IDs from the allowed list `cmd/spokesd/application.go`.
* `error: ...` - For twirp errors (status >= 400), the error message that is returned to the client.
* `http_version: HTTP/1.1` The client's HTTP version. Clients using TLS authentication may use HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2. Clients using HMAC auth may use HTTP/1.1.
* `level: ERROR` - Normally either INFO or ERROR. On `msg=request` log lines, ERROR means the status is >= 400.
* `msg: request` - The log message. 
* `quality_of_service: QUALITY_OF_SERVICE_...` - The QOS set by the client. DELAYABLE, FAIL_FAST, NO_DELAY are valid options. We currently allow INVALID, also.
* `remote_addr: 10.125.5.0:3923` - The remote address observed by spokesd. Note that this may not be the address of the client due to the routing mesh we use in production.
* `request_delay: 0` - The amount of delay added to the request by gitmon.
* `request_duration: 13.777865` - The time in milliseconds, measured by a Twirp hook from within the handler. See also `response_time`.
* `request_id: ...` - The request ID provided by the client.
* `request_method: POST` - The HTTP request method.
* `request_url: /twirp/github.spokes.objects.v1.ObjectsAPI/ResolveObject` - The HTTP request path.
* `response_time: 16.811607` - The time in milliseconds, measured from outside the Go HTTP request handler.
* `sha: 85084c8db8e89ecc9fc14c66e08fbec09c2448bd` - The current version of spokesd.
* `spec: 434602838/462876665` - The spec of the request's repository.
* `status: 404` - The HTTP response status.
* `twirp_method: ResolveObject` - The Twirp method that was called.
* `twirp_package: github.spokes.objects.v1` - The Twirp package that was called.
* `twirp_service: ObjectsAPI` - The Twirp API that was called.
* `user_agent: launch-worker/52a6374b1c25d79406f8c46e09489eb2524dd2c0` - The User-Agent string provided by the client.

### GitRPCd

These are selected fields from a typical `msg=request` log entry from gitrpcd.
This example omits common log fields (e.g. `site`, `kube_namespace`, `host`).
Note that this example comes from before a change to use semantic conventions.

* `CONTAINER_ID: ...`, `CONTAINER_ID_FULL: ...` - The ID of the docker container that is running this copy of GitRPCd. This is generated by Docker when the container is created.
* `CONTAINER_NAME: gitrpcd-20230724011711` - The name of the docker container that is running this copy of GitRPCd. This is generated by `deploy-gitrpcd.sh` when GitRPCd is deployed.
* `IMAGE_NAME: 702486989568.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/gitrpcd:40ff27fafebf553ca4f91dc5b63551af5779ac28` - The name of the docker image that was deployed.
* `cabinet: 0111` - The rack where this host is mounted.
* `component: twirp` - An indication of which part of GitRPCd generated the message.
* `http_version: HTTP/2.0` - The client's HTTP version. This is expected to be HTTP/2 for dotcom and HTTP/1.1 everywhere else.
* `level: INFO` - Normally either INFO or ERROR. On `msg=request` log lines, ERROR means the status is >= 400.
* `msg: request` - The log message.
* `remote_addr: 10.48.120.53:7120` - The remote address observed by gitrpcd.
* `request_duration: 3.514981` - The time in milliseconds, measured by a Twirp hook within the HTTP request handler.
* `request_id: ...` - The request ID provided by the client.
* `service: objects` - Identifies which service in the `services/` directory handled this request.
* `spec: 444622364/475103264` - The spec of the request's repository.
* `tls_client: blackbird-production` - Identifier of the client app. This will be one of the client IDs from spokesd's allowed list `cmd/spokesd/application.go`.
* `twirp_method: ResolveObject` The Twirp method that was called.
* `twirp_package: github.spokes.objects.v1` - The Twirp package that was called.
* `twirp_service: ObjectsAPI` - The Twirp API that was called.
* `twirp_status: 200` - The HTTP response status.
* `user_agent: blackbird-ingest/e45aa492d05162d9c76691322d739c09d5a09ffd spokesd/85084c8db8e89ecc9fc14c66e08fbec09c2448bd` - The User-Agent string provided by spokesd. This is usually the client's User-Agent plus "spokesd/$version".

## Gitmon (governor)

* `spokesctl gov aggregate program count -t1h -V gitrpcd` - Count requests by
  endpoint in the last hour. Spokes Access API calls and any git process that
  is spawned are "via gitrpcd".

## Lightstep

Spokesd and GitRPCd both record spans.

### Finding a caller

Sometimes it's useful to trace back from a Spokesd or GitRPCd span to a span in the caller, in order to find more information about the caller. For example, to find a background worker that's calling ResolveObject with the "delayable" QOS, start a [new lightstep notebook](https://app.lightstep.com/github-prod/notebooks), switch to the Query editor, and paste in this query:

```
spans_sample service == "spokesd" && spokes_quality_of_service == "QUALITY_OF_SERVICE_DELAYABLE" && operation == "ResolveObject"
| assemble
| trace_filter service == "github-aqueduct-worker" || service == "github-unicorn-api" || service == "github-actionsworker" || service == "github-stream-processor"
```

Choose to View as "Scatter plot".

Or see the [Delayable Spokes Access API calls from the monolith](https://app.lightstep.com/github-prod/dashboard/ZmtL3DvY) notebook.
